# Packages installations

```{r}
# Install only the packages that are missing (CRAN + Bioconductor)
cran_pkgs <- c("megatrees", "piggyback", "ape", "caper", "phytools",
               "ggplot2", "ggnewscale", "dplyr", "tidyr")
bioc_pkgs <- c("ggtree", "ggtreeExtra", "treeio")

missing_cran <- setdiff(cran_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing_cran) > 0) install.packages(missing_cran)

missing_bioc <- setdiff(bioc_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing_bioc) > 0) {
  if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
  BiocManager::install(missing_bioc, ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
}

# Paths: input data are read from data/, results are written to output/
data_dir <- "data"
out_dir  <- "output"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r}
  "Mustela_putorius_furo"    = "Mustela_putorius",
  "Rhinopoma_cystops"        = "Rhinopoma_hardwickii",
  "Dasypus_beniensis"        = "Dasypus_novemcinctus",
  "Osphranter_rufus"         = "Macropus_rufus",
  "Notamacropus_rufogriseus" = "Macropus_rufogriseus",
  "Equus_asinus"             = "Equus_africanus",
  "Saimiri_cassiquiarensis"  = "Saimiri_sciureus"
)

# We drop this species since we already have the data for the closest species

  "Cervus_hanglu_bactrianus",
```

```{r}
library(ape)
library(caper)


# Load curated data and pruned 100 trees if not already loaded
data_pgls <- read.csv(
  file.path(out_dir, "PGLS_data_curated_Upham.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

pruned_trees <- read.tree(
  file.path(out_dir, "Upham_100trees_pruned_curated_species.tre")
)

# Function to run one PGLS model on one tree
run_pgls_one_tree <- function(tree, data, response_col) {
  
  # Reorder data to match tree tip order - by name
  data2 <- data[match(tree$tip.label, data$tree_species), ]
  
  # Check that matching worked
  stopifnot(nrow(data2) == length(tree$tip.label))
  stopifnot(all(tree$tip.label == data2$tree_species))
  
  # Build comparative dataset for caper::pgls
  comp <- comparative.data(
    phy = tree,
    data = data2,
    names.col = tree_species,
    vcv = TRUE,
    warn.dropped = FALSE
  )
  
  # Model formula: response variable ~ log brain volume
  form <- as.formula(paste(response_col, "~ X"))
  
  # Run PGLS with Pagel's lambda estimated by ML
  fit <- pgls(
    form,
    data = comp,
    lambda = "ML"
  )
  
  s <- summary(fit)
  
  # Extract model statistics for the effect of X
  
  data.frame(
    response = response_col,
    lambda = fit$param["lambda"],
    slope = s$coefficients["X", "Estimate"],
    SE = s$coefficients["X", "Std. Error"],
    t = s$coefficients["X", "t value"],
    p = s$coefficients["X", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    R2 = s$r.squared
  )
}

# Run each PGLS model across all 100 pruned trees and combine the results
# Y ~ X = heat capacity ~ log brain volume
# Z ~ X = susceptibility ~ log brain volume
# W ~ X = metastability ~ log brain volume

responses <- c("Y", "Z", "W")

results_100 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(responses, function(resp) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(pruned_trees), function(i) {
    out <- run_pgls_one_tree(pruned_trees[[i]], data_pgls, resp)
    out$tree_number <- i
    out
  }))
}))

# Save full results
write.csv(
  results_100,
  file.path(out_dir, "PGLS_results_100_Upham_trees.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Summarize across trees with 95% quantile ranges
q025 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
q975 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)

# Summarize PGLS results across the 100 trees
summary_100 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(results_100, results_100$response), function(df) {
  data.frame(
    response = unique(df$response),
    n_trees = nrow(df),
    
    lambda_median = median(df$lambda, na.rm = TRUE),
    lambda_q025 = q025(df$lambda),
    lambda_q975 = q975(df$lambda),
    
    slope_median = median(df$slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    slope_q025 = q025(df$slope),
    slope_q975 = q975(df$slope),
    
    SE_median = median(df$SE, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    p_median = median(df$p, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_q025 = q025(df$p),
    p_q975 = q975(df$p),
    p_max = max(df$p, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    R2_median = median(df$R2, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}))

print(summary_100)

write.csv(
  summary_100,
  file.path(out_dir, "PGLS_summary_100_Upham_trees_quantile_ranges.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

# Consensus tree



```{r}
# ============================================================
# HALF-CIRCLE CONSENSUS TREE FIGURE  (publication version)
#
# Tree:
#   50% majority-rule consensus of the 100 time-calibrated Upham trees, with
#   median divergence times mapped back onto the consensus topology (branch
#   lengths are real ages in Myr; tree is ultrametric so tips align).
#
# Rings (inner -> outer):
#   Inner ring   : log2 brain volume   (viridis scale; slightly thicker)
#   Outer ring 1 : Heat capacity
#   Outer ring 2 : Susceptibility
#   Outer ring 3 : Metastability        (shared blue-white-red diverging scale)
# ============================================================

library(ape)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtree)
library(ggtreeExtra)
library(ggnewscale)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(grid)

# ============================================================
# Paths
# ============================================================

tree_file <- file.path(out_dir, "Upham_100trees_pruned_curated_species.tre")
data_file <- file.path(out_dir, "PGLS_data_curated_Upham.csv")

out_pdf <- file.path(out_dir, "Consensus_Upham_tree_paper.pdf")
out_png <- file.path(out_dir, "Consensus_Upham_tree_paper.png")

# ============================================================
# Read trees and data
# ============================================================

trees <- read.tree(tree_file)
class(trees) <- "multiPhylo"

cat("Number of trees:", length(trees), "\n")
cat("Tips in first tree:", length(trees[[1]]$tip.label), "\n")

df <- read.csv(data_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

if (!"tree_species" %in% colnames(df)) {
  stop("Column 'tree_species' was not found.")
}

# Fix names to the tree-name format
df$Species <- gsub(" ", "_", df$tree_species)

# Keep only rows retained for PGLS, just in case
if ("drop_from_pgls" %in% colnames(df)) {
  keep_idx <- is.na(df$drop_from_pgls) |
    df$drop_from_pgls %in% c(FALSE, "FALSE", "False", 0, "0")
  df <- df[keep_idx, ]
}

required_cols <- c("Species", "X", "Y", "Z", "W")
missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, colnames(df))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop(paste("Missing required columns:", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
}

df <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(Species), !is.na(X), !is.na(Y), !is.na(Z), !is.na(W)) %>%
  distinct(Species, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("Species in data after filtering:", nrow(df), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Build majority-rule consensus tree
# ============================================================

cons_tree <- consensus(trees, p = 0.5)

common_species <- intersect(cons_tree$tip.label, df$Species)
cat("Species shared between consensus tree and data:", length(common_species), "\n")

cons_tree <- drop.tip(cons_tree, setdiff(cons_tree$tip.label, common_species))

df <- df %>% filter(Species %in% common_species)
df <- df[match(cons_tree$tip.label, df$Species), ]
stopifnot(all(df$Species == cons_tree$tip.label))

# Rearrange branch order for a cleaner ladder
cons_tree <- ladderize(cons_tree, right = FALSE)
df <- df[match(cons_tree$tip.label, df$Species), ]
stopifnot(all(df$Species == cons_tree$tip.label))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Real (time-calibrated) branch lengths for the consensus topology
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# The majority-rule consensus carries no branch lengths. Rather than invent
# arbitrary ones, map median divergence times from the 100 time-calibrated
# Upham trees onto the consensus topology: for each internal node take its
# descendant-tip set, find that set's MRCA in each of the 100 trees, read the
# MRCA's age (time before present), and assign the median across trees. Tips are
# fixed at age 0, so the tree is ultrametric (tips aligned -> clean rings) and
# every branch length is a median divergence time in millions of years.
# Because each consensus node's tip set is a superset of its children's, its
# MRCA is an ancestor of theirs in every tree, so ages are monotone down the
# tree and all branch lengths are non-negative.
add_consensus_divergence_times <- function(cons, trees) {
  ntip   <- length(cons$tip.label)
  inodes <- (ntip + 1):(ntip + cons$Nnode)

  # descendant tip labels of each consensus internal node
  desc <- lapply(inodes, function(nd) extract.clade(cons, nd)$tip.label)

  # age (time before present) of every node, per tree
  tree_age <- lapply(trees, function(tr) {
    d <- node.depth.edgelength(tr)   # root-to-node distance
    max(d) - d                       # -> time before present (tips ~ 0)
  })

  # median MRCA age across the 100 trees for each consensus node
  age <- numeric(ntip + cons$Nnode)  # tips stay 0
  for (k in seq_along(inodes)) {
    tips_k <- desc[[k]]
    ages_k <- vapply(seq_along(trees), function(i) {
      tree_age[[i]][getMRCA(trees[[i]], tips_k)]
    }, numeric(1))
    age[inodes[k]] <- median(ages_k, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  # branch length = parent age - child age (>= 0 by construction)
  cons$edge.length <- age[cons$edge[, 1]] - age[cons$edge[, 2]]
  cons
}

cons_tree <- add_consensus_divergence_times(cons_tree, trees)

stopifnot(all(cons_tree$edge.length >= 0))   # no negative branches
cat("Root age (median across 100 trees, Myr):",
    round(max(node.depth.edgelength(cons_tree)), 1), "\n")
cat("Final number of species in figure:", nrow(df), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Display labels: underscores -> spaces
# ============================================================

label_df <- data.frame(
  Species       = df$Species,
  Species_label = gsub("_", " ", df$Species),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# ============================================================
# Ring data
# ============================================================

# Inner thick ring: log2 brain volume (original scale)
x_ring <- df %>%
  transmute(Species = Species, Ring = "log2 brain volume", Value = X)

# Three outer rings, each trait scaled independently
# (0 = average, + = high, - = low) so they share one diverging scale
outer_rings <- df %>%
  transmute(
    Species          = Species,
    `Heat capacity`  = as.numeric(scale(Y)),
    `Susceptibility` = as.numeric(scale(Z)),
    `Metastability`  = as.numeric(scale(W))
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Heat capacity`, `Susceptibility`, `Metastability`),
    names_to = "Ring", values_to = "Value"
  )

outer_rings$Value[is.na(outer_rings$Value)] <- 0

outer_rings$Ring <- factor(
  outer_rings$Ring,
  levels = c("Heat capacity", "Susceptibility", "Metastability")
)

trait_lim <- max(abs(outer_rings$Value), na.rm = TRUE)

# ----- alignment safety checks -----
stopifnot(setequal(x_ring$Species, cons_tree$tip.label))
stopifnot(all(table(x_ring$Species) == 1))
stopifnot(setequal(outer_rings$Species, cons_tree$tip.label))
stopifnot(all(table(outer_rings$Species) == 3))
cat("Ring alignment checks passed.\n")

# ============================================================
# Base tree
# ============================================================

p <- ggtree(cons_tree, layout = "fan", open.angle = 180)

p$data <- p$data %>%
  left_join(label_df, by = c("label" = "Species"))


tree_depth   <- max(node.depth.edgelength(cons_tree))
lab_offset   <- 0.45 * tree_depth   # labels just past the outer ring
brain_pwidth <- 0.14 * tree_depth   # single-category inner ring (absolute width)

p <- p +
  geom_tree(color = "grey45", linewidth = 0.72) +
  geom_tiplab2(
    aes(label = Species_label),
    size     = 2.0,
    offset   = lab_offset,   # past the outer ring, hugging the arc
    align    = FALSE,
    linesize = 0,
    fontface = "italic"
  )

# ============================================================
# Legend sizing
# ============================================================

legend_bar_width  <- unit(120, "pt")
legend_bar_height <- unit(8, "pt")

# ============================================================
# Inner thick ring: log2 brain volume
# ============================================================

p <- p +
  geom_fruit(
    data    = x_ring,
    geom    = geom_tile,
    mapping = aes(y = Species, x = Ring, fill = Value),
    offset  = 0.040,       # close to the tree tips
    pwidth  = brain_pwidth, # absolute width (scaled to tree depth); ~slightly thicker than each trait arc
    color     = "grey93",
    linewidth = 0.08,
    grid.params = list()
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    # Viridis (purple -> teal -> green -> yellow). The green/teal band does not
    # occur in the blue-white-red trait scale, so the inner ring is clearly a
    # different colour scheme rather than looking like another trait ring.
    colours = c("#440154", "#414487", "#2A788E", "#22A884", "#7AD151", "#FDE725"),
    limits  = range(x_ring$Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    name    = "Inner thick ring: log2 brain volume",
    guide   = guide_colorbar(
      direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0,
      barwidth = legend_bar_width, barheight = legend_bar_height
    )
  )

# ============================================================
# Outer rings: Heat capacity, Susceptibility, Metastability
# ============================================================

p <- p +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_fruit(
    data    = outer_rings,
    geom    = geom_tile,
    mapping = aes(y = Species, x = Ring, fill = Value),
    offset  = 0.010,   # close to the inner brain ring
    # Three equal trait arcs: total band 0.24 -> 0.08 each, slightly thinner
    # than the brain ring so the inner (key) variable reads as slightly thicker.
    pwidth  = 0.24,
    color     = "grey94",
    linewidth = 0.08,
    grid.params = list()
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-trait_lim, trait_lim),
    name   = "Outer rings, inner → outer:\nHeat capacity, Susceptibility, Metastability",
    breaks = c(-trait_lim, 0, trait_lim),
    labels = c("Low", "Average", "High"),
    guide  = guide_colorbar(
      direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0,
      barwidth = legend_bar_width, barheight = legend_bar_height
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    caption = paste(
      "Grey branches = majority-rule consensus phylogeny.",
      "Thick inner ring = log2 brain volume.",
      "Outer rings, inner to outer = heat capacity, susceptibility, metastability."
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.box        = "horizontal",
    legend.box.just   = "center",
    legend.justification = "center",
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 8.5),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
    # Room for the (now unclipped) tip labels to render past the panel edge.
    plot.margin       = margin(t = 30, r = 30, b = 8, l = 30),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0.10, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.x   = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.margin      = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)
  )


p$coordinates$clip <- "off"

# ============================================================
# Save figure, with a to-scale time scale bar in the bottom legend area
# ============================================================

fig_w <- 12; fig_h <- 8
bar_Myr <- 50


# 0.152 = fraction of the page width spanned by the tree depth (172.6 Myr)
# in this 12 x 8 in figure. Re-measure if the figure size or the tree changes.
npc_per_Myr <- 0.152 / 172.6

draw_scalebar <- function() {
  print(p)
  bar_npc <- bar_Myr * npc_per_Myr
  cx <- 0.5; by <- 0.30; th <- 0.012        # centre-x, baseline-y, tick height (npc)
  gp <- gpar(lwd = 2.5, col = "black", lineend = "butt")
  grid.lines(unit(c(cx - bar_npc/2, cx + bar_npc/2), "npc"), unit(c(by, by), "npc"), gp = gp)
  grid.lines(unit(c(cx - bar_npc/2, cx - bar_npc/2), "npc"), unit(c(by, by + th), "npc"), gp = gp)
  grid.lines(unit(c(cx + bar_npc/2, cx + bar_npc/2), "npc"), unit(c(by, by + th), "npc"), gp = gp)
  grid.text(paste(bar_Myr, "Myr"), unit(cx, "npc"), unit(by - 0.028, "npc"),
            gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, col = "black"))
}

png(out_png, width = fig_w, height = fig_h, units = "in", res = 600); draw_scalebar(); dev.off()
pdf(out_pdf, width = fig_w, height = fig_h);                          draw_scalebar(); dev.off()
```

# Blomberg's K

```{r}
library(phytools)

# Blomberg's K across the same 100 trees and same data used for PGLS
# X = log brain volume
# Y = heat capacity
# Z = susceptibility
# W = metastability

# The p-values come from random permutations, so they vary slightly between
# runs. The values reported in the paper are in results_published/.

# Function to calculate Blomberg's K for one trait on one tree
run_K_one_tree <- function(tree, data, trait_col, nsim = 999) {
  
  # Match the data order to the order of species in the tree
  data2 <- data[match(tree$tip.label, data$tree_species), ]
  
  # Safety checks: same logic as in the PGLS function
  stopifnot(!any(is.na(data2$tree_species)))
  stopifnot(nrow(data2) == length(tree$tip.label))
  stopifnot(all(tree$tip.label == data2$tree_species))
  
  # Create a named vector of trait values, with species names as labels
  trait_vec <- setNames(data2[[trait_col]], data2$tree_species)
  
  # Calculate Blomberg's K and test significance by simulation
  K_result <- phylosig(
    tree,
    trait_vec,
    method = "K",
    test = TRUE,
    nsim = nsim
  )
  
  # Return the trait name, K value, and p-value
  data.frame(
    trait = trait_col,
    K = as.numeric(K_result$K),
    p = as.numeric(K_result$P)
  )
}

# Traits for which Blomberg's K will be calculated
traits <- c("X", "Y", "Z", "W")

# Run Blomberg's K for each trait across all 100 trees
K_results_100 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(traits, function(trait_name) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(pruned_trees), function(i) {
    out <- run_K_one_tree(
      tree = pruned_trees[[i]],
      data = data_pgls,
      trait_col = trait_name,
      # Randomly shuffle the trait values across the tips 999 times
      nsim = 999
    )
    # Add the tree number so results can be traced back to each tree
    out$tree_number <- i
    out
  }))
}))

# Save full results
write.csv(
  K_results_100,
  file.path(out_dir, "Blombergs_K_results_100_Upham_trees.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Summarize across trees
q025 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
q975 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)

K_summary_100 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(K_results_100, K_results_100$trait), function(df) {
  data.frame(
    trait = unique(df$trait),
    n_trees = nrow(df),
    
    K_median = median(df$K, na.rm = TRUE),
    K_q025 = q025(df$K),
    K_q975 = q975(df$K),
    
    p_median = median(df$p, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_q025 = q025(df$p),
    p_q975 = q975(df$p),
    p_max = max(df$p, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}))

print(K_summary_100)

write.csv(
  K_summary_100,
  file.path(out_dir, "Blombergs_K_summary_100_Upham_trees.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
